title: Showcase: launch day
summary: Launch the water rocket with the stable fin design, and show the flight data and the drone frame's thrust result on a board.
materials: the water rocket, launcher and stable fins from weeks 5 and 6
the printed drone frame with its four motors dry-fitted (no propellers) from week 7
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
safety glasses for everyone at the launch
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 5 through 7

steps.title: Plan launch day
steps.body:
Write the season's flight numbers on the board, large enough to read from across the yard. Include the best water volume from week 5 and the fin size that swung stable from week 6. Add the Earth's surface orbital speed from week 7, and the drone frame's measured thrust-to-weight ratio.

Plan the presentation in this order.

1. Show the swing test that proved the fins stable before anything ever launched.

2. Launch the rocket once for the family, at the water volume and pump strokes that flew best.

3. Show the printed drone frame with its four motors dry-fitted, and state its thrust-to-weight ratio.

4. Show the board's numbers, including how the ball-on-a-string speed compared with a real orbit.

5. Answer one question from the family about the fins or the frame's 250 gram weight budget.

Everyone at the launch, family included, wears safety glasses. No propeller goes on the frame today; it is shown mounted, not spun.

figure.alt: A showcase layout with three items left to right: the fair board with the season's numbers (step 4), the rocket on its launcher with stable fins (step 2, launched live), and the printed drone frame with its four motors dry-fitted and no propellers (step 3, its thrust-to-weight ratio stated). Captions note the swing test is shown before the launch, and everyone wears safety glasses.

steps.title: Rehearse the launch
steps.body:
With an adult, do one test launch at demo settings before the family watches, using the same water volume and pump strokes the data recommended.

Practise saying the orbit comparison out loud, plainly. State the ball's real measured speed, and how many times slower that is than the 7.9 kilometres per second an orbit needs.

Practise stating the drone frame's thrust-to-weight ratio in one sentence, and where each gram in its weight budget went.
checklist: The board shows the season's real numbers from weeks 5 through 7
A test launch at demo settings succeeded before the family saw it
Everyone who will be at the launch has safety glasses ready
I can state the swing speed versus orbital speed comparison in one sentence
The printed drone frame is ready to show, motors dry-fitted and no propellers attached

steps.title: Launch day
steps.body:
Gather the family at a safe distance, with everyone wearing safety glasses. Show the swing test result, then launch the rocket once with an adult operating the release.

After it lands, show the printed drone frame and state its thrust-to-weight ratio. Show the board's numbers and answer one question about the fins or the frame's weight budget.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the launch, a photo of the board with the season's numbers, and a photo of the drone frame with its motors
